newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Swedish PM sees new EMU conflicts.
newsitem.headline: Swedish PM sees new EMU conflicts.

text.p: Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson has warned that conflicts still lie ahead for the European Union on the path to economic and monetary union (EMU).
Persson was speaking to reporters late on Friday after EU leaders, meeting in Dublin, agreed on a pact to ensure fiscal discipline within EMU.
"I think we will see that we will come back to new...conflicts, new difficult decisions," he said.
He said one of the "absolutely most difficult decisions" would be choosing which countries should join EMU.
EU leaders are due to decide in early 1998 which countries qualify for EMU under the economic convergence criteria which were laid down in the EU's Maastricht Treaty.

Persson said the agreement on the stability pact to curb budget deficits within EMU was "okay" for Sweden but that it remained to be seen how it would be received in Germany and France. "I think it was the best decision we could get."
